findings.text: The root package.json postinstall 'install-electron' runs on every pnpm install, including `pnpm install --prod` or any install where devDependencies are skipped. In those cases the electron bin is missing and the install fails with command-not-found. Both CI jobs running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` will now also download the Electron binary, around 100 MB per job, unless it is cached. A guard such as an ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD-style env check, or tolerating a missing bin, would limit this.

Electron 45 has no install script of its own (its package.json has bin install-electron but no scripts.postinstall). So the 'electron' entry in onlyBuiltDependencies does nothing, and the binary actually comes from the root postinstall. The test contract still requires the allowlist, so this is fine as written.

The test contract says onlyBuiltDependencies must be exactly ['electron','esbuild']. The spec's yamlList helper checks this in order, and also rejects dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds, onlyBuiltDependenciesFile and a pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies override in package.json, which is more than the contract asks.
`packages: 'external'` already makes electron external. The explicit `external: ['electron']` repeats it, which does no harm.

launch.ts attaches its stdout/stderr listeners (collectOutput) only after _electron.launch resolves. If main prints the listening line before then, that output is never seen and waitForListening times out. It depends on Playwright's loader holding back app ready; reading the line through a listener attached at spawn, or Playwright's own process output, would remove the race.

build-desktop.spec 'playwright config split' calls createFileMatcher from playwright/lib/util. That is an internal module, even though the package exports it, so a Playwright minor bump could rename or reshape it and break this vitest check with no matching change in behaviour.

The 'launcher env' test catches a process.env spread by checking the harness's own env keys against the allowlist (desktop.env). The checks on main's process.env alone would not catch one, because serverEnv overrides DATABASE_URL and the key and drops ORIGIN anyway. Both layers are asserted, so the contract holds.
e2e/desktop/*.ts is not in tsconfig include; only playwright.desktop.config.ts was added, as the task specified. This matches the existing e2e/ files, which are not included either.

The contract's 30s first-window bound is not enforced end to end. launchDesktop waits up to 30s for the listening line, then firstWindow, toHaveURL and toBeVisible each get their own 30s, and the desktop config's test timeout is 90s. A first launch taking 40-90s would still pass first-run.e2e.

quitThroughApp awaits app.evaluate(({ app }) => app.quit()). If the main process's shutdown is ever fast enough to close the Playwright connection before the evaluate reply arrives, evaluate rejects and the test fails on a clean quit. Firing the quit without awaiting the evaluate result, or catching a 'closed' rejection, would remove the race.
The test process inserts the watch while launch 1 holds the DB, and the app has no WAL or busy timeout. This is safe only because the scheduler is disabled and the UI is idle at that moment.
The key is only ever compared by hash or decoded length and never printed. The ntfy topic and the watch URL are on .invalid hosts and the scheduler stays disabled, so r-01 and r-03 hold.
Every 403 case is checked two ways: CSRF refusals must contain Kit's CSRF text, and Host refusals must have the body 'Forbidden'. So a 403 from the wrong layer cannot pass by accident.

The four tests in the 'guard in the app window' block share one app launch. This only works because the desktop config sets workers: 1 and fullyParallel: false, and test 1's saved ntfy channel is part of the 'before' snapshot that test 2 compares against.

On macOS and Windows the 'login launch is tray-only' test reads app.getLoginItemSettings() for the unpackaged electron binary, which reflects the host machine's real login-item state; a developer machine that once registered Electron would fail this check for reasons unrelated to the app

The login-launch test waits for the 'activate' listener to be attached before asserting no window, which ties the check to lifecycle.ts's startup order and keeps it from passing vacuously while startup is still running

The 'stopped' guard in tick() makes the 'interval stays armed after stop' assertions vacuous: removing clearInterval from stop() would not fail 'stop drains' or 'ticks every 5 minutes until stopped', since every later tick returns null. A timer-count assertion (e.g. vi.getTimerCount()) would pin the interval teardown itself.
In hooks.server.ts, closeDb reads db.$client only inside the closure, so publishing during a build never touches the build-time db Proxy.

Once stop() hits its drainMs timeout it resolves with a pass still running, so a quit that calls closeDb next will close the db under that pass. This is the accepted trade-off of the drain bound, and it is logged.

alerts-key.spec 'a damaged key created by a competitor mid-write' asserts the path is named but never asserts the error message/stack omits the file contents ('half-writ'); the no-leak check exists only in the 'bad key refused' table
server-env.spec 'awkward path' uses process.chdir, which works only because Vitest 4 defaults to the forks pool; switching the server project to pool 'threads' would make it throw

databaseUrl's claim that Windows drive letters and backslashes pass through libsql unescaped is exercised only by the POSIX awkward-path test; Windows CI is the only place that path shape gets checked
The two 'close with keep-alive' tests start their servers without pushing them onto `started`, so if an assertion fails before `server.close()` the listening server leaks into later tests.
loadAdapterHandler replaces process.env instead of merging into it. Callers must pass a complete environment, which serverEnv already builds from the inherited env.

The tests go beyond the contract: they also cover a handler that throws (500), next() (404), and a repeated X-Forwarded-Proto header line, and the rawHeaders rewrite stops headersDistinct from bringing the client value back.

will-navigate to an off-origin http(s) URL also hands it to shell.openExternal. The task description only says such navigations are prevented, but this matches the external_links decision and is tested.

The test 'never cancels close' exercises createMainWindow, which registers no 'close' listener, so it can only catch a listener added there. A close listener added in showWindow would still be caught indirectly, because 'creates exactly one new window after the old one was closed' would then fail.
windowOptions also sets webviewTag:false, beyond the stated preferences. It is a harmless hardening.

Description asks the executor to confirm wasOpenedAtLogin still reports on macOS 13+ with the pinned Electron (45.2.3) and record the finding; the recorded finding in login-item.ts says it is unconfirmed. The window-at-login fallback is safe, but tray-only login launch on packaged macOS is still unconfirmed.

linux ensureRegisteredOnce: if the autostart entry is written but the marker write then fails, the outcome is 'failed' with the entry left in place; the next launch just rewrites it, so this is harmless.

toggleLogin computes the new value from a fresh loginItem.isEnabled() call rather than from the clicked item's checked state, so a toggle always flips whatever the OS currently reports; the 'toggles back and forth' and 'policy pin' tests pin this down
the test 'the macOS file name ends in Template.png' only checks a constant against itself; the real guarantee comes from the darwin icon-path test and the file-exists test
the RealDeps -> TrayDeps<Menu> assignment in tray.spec.ts is only checked at compile time (pnpm check); vitest alone will not catch drift from Electron's Tray/Menu types

A before-quit that arrives during startup (before running.server/runtime are set, e.g. while startServer is still opening the DB) runs an empty shutdown and calls app.exit(0) right away, so the server and DB are never closed cleanly. Exiting the process releases them, so this is a rare-path risk rather than a bug, but no test covers quitting mid-startup.
If startServer resolves but readRuntime throws, the listening server is never closed before app.exit(1). Process exit cleans it up, and the 'unpublished runtime' test covers the exit path.

The window-all-closed test spoofs process.platform across win32/linux/darwin, but the handler ignores platform, so the per-platform runs differ only in name. They still guard against a future platform-specific regression.
The realDepsFit compile-time check, which confirms Electron's real App/PowerMonitor/Dialog fit the structural deps, is only enforced by pnpm check, not by vitest.

build-desktop.spec 'real entry' matches the identifier `moduleUrl` inside the bundled import() call; esbuild keeps that name today but would rename it on a scope collision, which would fail the test even though the bundle is correct
ICON_DIR resolves to <appRoot>/src/desktop/assets, so packaging must ship src/desktop/assets alongside dist-desktop; outside this task's scope
installAppMenu runs only after runDesktop resolves 'started'; until then macOS shows Electron's default menu, which also has Quit, so no gap in behaviour
